business_review.text: Form validation errors announced by screen readers on the listed modals/pages (WCAG SC 4.1.3, SC 3.3.1) by aligning Input, Select, MultiSelect with Textarea pattern.
Computed ARIA values win over caller-supplied aria-invalid/aria-describedby.

standards_review.standard: git-workflow: EPMCDME-XXXX_ prefix on branch and commits
standards_review.notes: Branch EPMCDME-8489_a11y-form-error-live-region; 4 commits all prefixed EPMCDME-8489:
Change is ARIA attribute wiring only, no user-input rendering.

findings.problem: aria-describedby={error ? errorId : undefined} is placed after {...rest}, which unconditionally overrides any caller-supplied aria-describedby. When no error is present the effective value is undefined, so React strips the attribute — silently losing hint/help associations passed by any of the 84 Input call sites that legitimately supply their own aria-describedby.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller renders alongside a Between 18 and 100. With no error, the current code sets aria-describedby={undefined}, removing the caller's association. Screen readers no longer announce the hint on focus.
findings.impact: WCAG 1.3.1 / 4.1.2 regression on any Input call site that provides its own aria-describedby; the fix's own guide currently claims 'caller-supplied ones are dropped by design', which frames a regression as intentional.
findings.recommendation: Merge the caller's aria-describedby with errorId when both are present: aria-describedby={[restDescribedBy, error ? errorId : undefined].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined}. Update the 'caller cannot override' Input test to assert merge behavior (caller's id + error id when error, caller's id alone when no error). Update form-patterns.md to reflect the actual contract (primitives always add the error id; they do not replace caller-supplied describedby).

findings.problem: role="alert" is announced by screen readers only on DOM insertion, not on text-content mutation. When the same field's error changes from one non-empty string to another (e.g. Yup revalidation replaces 'Required' with 'Min 3 chars'), the existing <div id=… role="alert"> stays in the DOM and only its text updates — VoiceOver/Safari and NVDA/Firefox do not re-announce.
findings.failure_scenario: User submits form empty → 'Required' announced. User types one character → RHF mode:onChange fires, error becomes 'Must be at least 3 characters'. Same div, mutated text; screen reader stays silent.
findings.impact: WCAG 4.1.3 fails on error refinements — the primary a11y scenario the ticket exists to fix. Applies to all three fixed primitives.
findings.recommendation: Add key={error} to the role="alert" div in Input.tsx, Select.tsx, and MultiSelect.tsx. React unmounts+remounts the div on every distinct error string, guaranteeing a fresh insertion announcement. No test change strictly required; a targeted assertion on the div's element identity across error changes is nice-to-have.

rationale: Blind lens raised the caller-override issue (CR-001) and two additional concerns that triage dismisses: (a) Select pt.input target — the T2 test already queries input[aria-haspopup="listbox"] and confirms attrs land on the focusable a11y input; (b) MultiSelect pt.input caller-merge — MultiSelect builds preparedPreset internally and does not accept a caller pt prop, so no merge path exists. Edge-case lens flagged the role="alert" text-mutation non-announcement in all three primitives (CR-002); the recommended fix (key={error}) is a one-line remount forcing insertion semantics. Acceptance lens confirmed 11/11 criteria met. Both surviving findings are patch-class (mechanical, no design decision) — fix and re-check.
